name: e6
responses: Past losses should not determine future policy by themselves. Continuing a failing or escalating course merely to “justify” deaths already incurred can produce even greater losses without improving security. Reassessment allows leaders to weigh current objectives, risks, alternatives, and the likelihood of success. This does not dishonor those who died; it treats their lives as a reason to make more careful decisions rather than as a commitment to continue regardless of changing circumstances.

Past losses should not determine future policy by themselves. The relevant question is whether continuing the commitment still advances achievable objectives at an acceptable cost, or whether changing course would better protect lives and security. Continuing solely to “justify” deaths already incurred risks compounding those losses without improving the strategic position. Reassessment can also honor service members by ensuring that further sacrifices are necessary rather than automatic.
